reading.body:
Tina Smith's AI record in this data is almost entirely one bill: S. 2296, which she voted against at every stage.

The pattern is lopsided. Thirteen of the fourteen events concern S. 2296, and twelve of those are procedural or amendment votes on a single day, 2025-10-09. She voted Nay on cloture, on the motion to proceed, on the motion to table, and on final passage. On the amendments she split, five Yea and four Nay, which is the only variation in the record. The two cosponsorships, S. 3682 and S. 2997, are the only affirmative legislative acts, and both are dated after the S. 2296 votes.

For AI specifically, the record shows opposition to the bill as a whole rather than a consistent position on its parts. A reader cannot tell from these entries what S. 2296 would have done, what the amendments changed, or whether her Nay votes reflected the bill's AI provisions or something else in it. The data carries no text of any bill and no stated rationale.

What this does not cover is as important as what it does. The summary mentions money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, but no contribution events appear in the points. There is no committee membership, no hearing record, no agency oversight, and no state-level activity. The page is a voting and cosponsorship log for one senator, and it should be read as that and nothing broader.
